insights.summary: AMD delivered exceptional Q2 2026 results with quarterly revenue of $11.5B (+50% YoY) driven by surging Data Center segment demand for EPYC CPUs and Instinct MI350 GPUs. Gross margin expanded dramatically to 54% from 40% YoY, with operating income swinging to $2.0B profit from a $134M loss, while the company secured major strategic partnerships with OpenAI and Meta committing to 6 gigawatts each of GPU deployments. Strong cash generation of $5.3B from operations and aggressive capex investment of $1.2B reflects confidence in AI-driven growth trajectory.
keyQuotes: Data Center net revenue of $6.7 billion for the three months ended June 27, 2026 increased by 107%, compared to net revenue of $3.2 billion for the prior year period...primarily driven by strong demand for our AMD EPYC processors and AMD Instinct MI350 Series GPUs.

In October 2025 and February 2026, we entered into multi-year agreements with OpenAI OpCo, LLC (OpenAI) and Meta Platforms, Inc. (Meta), respectively, under which each customer intends to deploy up to 6 gigawatts of AMD data center GPUs, with the first gigawatt of each deployment powered by our AMD Instinct MI450 series products.
The increase in both periods was primarily due to higher employee-related costs from an increase in headcount in support of our continued focus on our AI strategy and long-term growth opportunities.

insights.summary: AMD delivered strong full-year 2025 revenue growth of 34% to $34.6B, driven by robust demand for data center AI GPUs (MI350 Series) and EPYC processors, plus 51% growth in Client and Gaming. The company demonstrated pricing power and market share gains despite facing intense competition from Intel and Nvidia. Regulatory headwinds from U.S. export controls on MI308 products to China created a $440M net inventory charge, though partial reversal occurred in Q4 following license grants.
keyQuotes: In 2025, we delivered strong annual revenue growth with net revenue increasing 34% to $34.6 billion, compared to $25.8 billion in 2024. This growth was driven by the performance of our Data Center and Client and Gaming segments.

Data Center net revenue of $16.6 billion increased by 32% compared to $12.6 billion in 2024, primarily driven by strong demand for our 5th generation AMD EPYC™ processors and AMD Instinct™ MI350 Series GPUs.

In October 2025, we entered into a product purchase agreement with OpenAI OpCo, LLC, (OpenAI) to deploy 6 gigawatts of AMD GPUs, with the deployment of the first gigawatt of capacity powered by our AMD Instinct MI450 series products.

insights.summary: AMD delivered strong Q3 2025 results with revenue of $9.2B (+36% YoY) driven by robust demand for EPYC processors and MI350 GPUs in Data Center, and Ryzen processors plus gaming GPUs in Client & Gaming. Gross margin expanded to 52% despite $800M MI308 export control charges, while operating income reached $1.3B. The company is aggressively investing in AI capabilities through the ZT Systems acquisition and OpenAI partnership, with R&D spending up 31% and headcount expanding to support growth.
keyQuotes: The increase in net revenue was driven by an increase in Client and Gaming segment revenue, primarily driven by strong demand for our AMD Ryzen™ processors, semi-custom game console SoCs and Radeon™ gaming GPUs; and an increase in Data Center segment revenue primarily driven by strong demand for our 5th generation AMD EPYC™ processors and AMD Instinct™ MI350 Series GPUs.
The increase in both periods was due to higher employee-related costs from an increase in headcount in support of our continued focus on our AI strategy.

During the nine months ended September 27, 2025, we generated $5.1 billion of cash from operating activities and we returned $1.3 billion to stockholders through the repurchase of common stock under our Repurchase Program.

insights.summary: AMD achieved Q2 2025 revenue of $7.7B (+32% YoY) driven by strong Client/Gaming segment growth (69% YoY) and Data Center CPU sales, but gross margins compressed to 40% from 49% due to an $800M inventory charge related to U.S. export controls on MI308 GPUs. Net income of $872M benefited from an $853M tax benefit related to IRS approval of reasonable cause relief for dual consolidated losses, while underlying operational performance showed Data Center operating loss of $155M despite revenue growth.
keyQuotes: The increase in net revenue was driven by an increase in Client and Gaming segment revenue primarily driven by strong demand for the latest 'Zen 5' AMD Ryzen processors and higher semi-custom sales, and an increase in Data Center segment revenue primarily driven by growth in AMD EPYC CPU sales.

The decrease in gross margin was primarily due to approximately $800 million of inventory and related charges associated with the U.S. government export control on AMD Instinct MI308 Data Center GPU products.

On March 31, 2025, we completed the acquisition of ZT Group Int'l, Inc. (ZT Systems), which is expected to enable AMD to deliver end-to-end AI solutions and accelerate the design and deployment of AMD-powered AI infrastructure at scale optimized for the cloud.

insights.summary: AMD delivered strong Q2 2024 results with 9% YoY revenue growth to $5.8B and net income of $265M, driven by exceptional Data Center segment performance (115% YoY growth) from steep ramp of AMD Instinct GPU shipments and strong 4th Gen EPYC CPU sales. insights.summary: AMD reported Q3 2023 revenue of $5.8B (+4% YoY) with improved profitability: net income of $299M vs. $66M prior year, driven by strong Client segment growth (+42% revenue) as PC market improved and lower acquisition-related amortization. Management is actively investing in AI R&D (evidenced by 20% YoY increase in R&D spending and headcount expansion), signaling confidence in future opportunities despite current macro headwinds.
